[b]Blood in the Sand[/b]

The Astaniran Democratic Movement has accepted Qianxuns aid, even as the hammer and sickle stands ominously in the foreground of its backing. The Socialist Ethics Commission is pleased by developments and would submit the coded document back to general secretary Cui Fang. As Qianxun forces began to unload by the hundreds on the beaches of Democratic Astanir, the Weilai clique and the five minor parties of the Qianxun State Assembly could only hold their breaths as the state made ready to let Qianxun blood spill on foreign soil for the first time in its revolutionary history. But the time for drastic action is not yet.

[list]

How much longer for the planes? asked the woman, carefully cleaning the inside of her disassembled rifle.

At this rate, another week. the man replied as he put on his vest and inserted his ceramic plates. Dems took their sweet time with accepting freebies, so the ships had to wait and refuel.

Aww...

[/list]

The woman huffed before finally finishing her cleaning, raising her weapon up in the air, then shaking it haphazardly, letting the displaced dirt and grime accumulated within to fall to the floor in a thin pile. Then, leaning into the mirror, she smiled to check if her face seemed presentable to the cameras, her sharpened teeth sticking out ominously in the glare of the rooms lights. Seemingly satisfied, she turned to the man again as she began reassembling her rifle.

[list]

This place looks rough. she says. Dems look like theyve just dug-in and were waiting for something good to happen. Ya think Emzep made the right decision in having us go here? I mean, I appreciate the paycheck, but...

But?

Well, we aint even sure the Dems are gonna let Emzep do what they want. Youve seen these guys right? They aint commies.

[/list]

The man sighed. Ultimately, this whole operation was a farce in a way. Qianxun had resolved to save what it determined to be the only chance for democracy on this war-torn island. But SummitONE knew differently. They will land their troops, planes will fly over the Astaniran skies, and aid will begin feeding the starving men, women, and children of the land, but only on the condition that they let the hammer and sickle strike down on the institutions that they were striving to protect.

But a SummitONE operative was above these petty squables. A SummitONE fighter was smart enough to identify the evil and hypocrisy but to permit it if it meant they can be paid and fed to fight another day. The man knew that and so simply shrugged. He had seen plenty of this before, after all. The mans name was David Cyriacus, callsign Chicken Little. He was the Vespurian vice-president of SummitONE Solutions and a vetaran of the Sikirskian Civil War, now a Qianxun soldier of fortune. He knew carnage and had fought in it before. 

[list]

At the end of the day, the job of SummitONE is to fight and die for our pay. Cyriacus says bluntly. Good decisions, bad decisions, let our employers sort out which is what. Were no active agent and we aint got to choose which way is gonna save the most folks.

You sound mighty philosophical for a child killer, Mr. Vice. The woman quipped, chuckling to herself. Whatever, look Ill do the job, but Emzep better stabilize things quickly. These Dems dont look like they know how to govern a household, let alone a country.

[/list]

As the woman finished speaking, a loud thump, and then a crunch. The doors of the small vessel swung open, falling firmly down onto the white sands of Astanir. They had arrived. Cyriacus looked at the woman clearly in the eye and nodded. Alright, operations manager Freya Moran. He says, The job is simple. Interchange with the Democratic movement using the operations teams well be sending you. We have 2,000 men from SummitONE, Qunarco, and Miwu, as well as enough foreign aid to keep the Shamatine continent fed for the next century. Distribute everything and effectively to every single person you see, dont bother with keeping tabs for repeat claimants. We want the Astanirans to think and believe that Qianxun has their back, when their own institutions could not.

[list]

Aye! Freya says, making a mock salute. And those agents Qianxun wanted us to bring along?

Let them do their thing. From here on out, you are not SummitONE, but Pax international. Do your job beautifully and in the morning well swap out the company water supply for champagne. Now, get the hell outta here.

[/list]

[b]Revolution by any means[/b]

The Qianxun diplomats, satisfied with this arrangement, would quickly arrive in Kuwalkti to present their offer of support. The man nominally heading the talks was a certain Qiu Guang, a nameless, faceless bureaucrat sent by the Min Zhu Party Central Committee. Rather than conducting the preliminary discussions with the Democratic forces through his own merit, Qiu would instead defer to a Vespurian man who had arrived with him, who didnt even wear the official Qianxun business attire, but rather an aid workers uniform. The man was David Cyriacus, who was the true representative of Qianxuns interests in Astanir and the actual head of Pax International [i]ex officio[/i] through his control of its largest component, SummitONE Solutions.

Cyriacuss request was simple: Independent control of the workers hell be bringing along onto Democratic territory, as well as permission for the Qianxun Socialist Republic to conduct field investigations into Astanirs local population to collate statistical data necessary to optimize its distribution of aid. In secret, however, these field investigations were to facilitate the construction of a socialist party in Astanir as per the demands of the Qianxun Socialist Ethics Commission.

The demands were audacious, especially for a power that had decided to intervene in the conflict only now. So audacious, that general secretary Cui Fang had warned Cyriacus that if the Democratic forces would not deny them, they would at least take precious time to come to a final decision. And so, as Cyriacus was conducting talks in Kuwalkti, in private he would give Pax International the greenlight to start unloading materials onto Astanir even without the Democratic Councils permission, forcing them into a [i]fait accompli[/i].

The rationale behind this move was simple: If aid was to be distributed prematurely, who was going to take it away? Here was a starving child, handed a hot meal by the generous Pax Intl aid workers. Who is to tell him that he wasnt supposed to receive it yet? And for the Democratic soldiers, here were Qianxuns latest inventory of tanks, medicine, ammunition, supplies. Is the Democratic Council supposed to say that these cannot be used for now, even as their frontlines continue to crumble in the face of the Junta and National Armys onslaught?

With the greenlight received, Pax International would land on Astaniran soil and quickly get to work. 

In total, the first Qianxun ships carried around 10,000 men, 2,000 of which were field technicians that were to attach itself to the Democratic forces. The so-called Chief of Field Operations for Pax Intl was a certain woman named Freya Moran, a notorious Vespurian contractor who won some degree of fame for her antics protecting the Bobian Republic from the Kaiserreich roughly a year ago. She was also part of the SummitONE squad that arrived in Sal-Baliz, but ultimately left early before actual military operations there began.

Her task was simple: Win hearts and minds in the Democratic territories, splatter hearts and minds everywhere else. Pax Intl brought along food and water aid, most of them MREs created during SummitONEs operations in Sal-Baliz, and thus were expected to perfectly fulfill the cultural sensitivities of the Astaniran people. Rather than transferring this aid to the Democratic forces and risking corruption, Pax Intl would resort to distributing aid themselves, distributing aid stamps which Astanirans could exchange for food and water, as well as aid certificates which could be exchanged for tents and building materials to help with housing.

On the military front, Pax Intl would organize its field technicians into four aid battalions and one headquarters. Most of Pax Intl armed forces would consist of Qianxun and Hsinyuan contractors, while the bulk of the active leadership and officers would actually be Elseyro-Vespurians, chiefly from the state of Norrhollow in which SummitONE is based at. Qianxun itself had specifically resolved to have the Vespurians be more visible than the Qianxun for this operation in order to better sell the idea that Pax International was an international humanitarian organization, but to what extent this facade could be sustained was left in the hands of public opinion.

Due to fueling issues, SummitONEs inventory jets will take a few more days to arrive at Astanir, and so Pax Intl would focus on its land capabilities first. In total, around 18 ZTQ-11 light tanks, 50 ZSL-93 APCs, and 31 ZBL-07 IFVs would be supplied by Qianxun for the preliminary phase of the operation, which would be roughly enough firepower to keep Pax Intl operational for at least two major battles, with more supplies arriving by the day. 65,000 more men are anticipated to arrive together with the rest of the shipments, in particular the Wuying-89 fighter jets, which shall be crucial in turning the tide of battle and helping the Democratic forces break out of its problematic pocket.

Elsewhere, Pax Intl would also deploy Qianxun agents from the Socialist Ethics Commission to investigate Astaniran political attitudes in Democratic territory, hoping to single out any intellectuals, labor activists, and industry leaders who were open and willing to head a left-leaning political party organized under Qianxuns political direction.
